frames.narration: On Friday 27 February 2026, Alice wants a weekly meeting with Ben and Room 4B. The API reads the busy intervals of all three for the next two weeks, one index range scan each, and merges them. Monday 09:00 to 10:00 New York time is free for everyone.

Alice saves the series. The API stores one row: DTSTART 2026-03-02 09:00 with TZID America/New_York, a duration of one hour, and RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO with no end. An outbox row is written in the same transaction.

The room is booked for the 12-month horizon: 52 Mondays, from 2 March 2026 to 22 February 2027, in one transaction. The exclusion constraint rejects it, because Room 4B is already booked on 13 April. Alice skips that date, which becomes an EXDATE of the series, and the other 51 bookings commit.

The relay publishes the outbox row. One consumer adds the meeting to Ben's calendar and writes 51 busy intervals for each of them, in UTC. The mailer sends Chen, a guest outside the company, an iMIP email with METHOD:REQUEST.

Reminder timers exist only for the next day or two of occurrences, so the rolling job creates these on Sunday 1 March. The first meeting is at 09:00 EST on 2 March, which is 14:00 UTC, so the 10-minute reminders for Alice and Ben fire at 13:50 UTC. Each timer is keyed by occurrence, attendee and offset, so a repeat of the message changes nothing.

A push message tells Ben's phone to sync. It sends its sync token 812 and gets back one new event and token 813. The rule is expanded in New York's zone: Ben sees 14:00 on 2 March, 13:00 from 9 to 23 March because the US changed its clocks on 8 March and the UK only on 29 March, and 14:00 again from 30 March.

Chen accepts in his own mail app, which sends an iMIP reply with PARTSTAT=ACCEPTED. The reply is matched by the event's UID, Chen is marked as attending, and the change gets the next number in Alice's change log, so her phone picks it up on its next sync.
